title: Strength Training for Total Beginners: The Only 5 Moves You Need
description: You do not need a complicated program to start lifting. Five basic movements, done consistently, build real strength. Here's how to begin.
excerpt: Forget the 20-exercise routine. Five compound movements, done twice a week, are all a beginner needs to get genuinely strong.
content:
Most beginners quit strength training because they overcomplicate it. They copy an advanced influencer's 20-exercise split, feel lost, and stop. The truth is simpler: a handful of basic movements, done consistently, will make you strong.

**The five movements that cover everything**

1. **Squat** — legs and core. Start with bodyweight, then add a barbell or dumbbells.
2. **Hinge (deadlift)** — back, glutes, hamstrings. The single most useful strength movement.
3. **Push (press)** — chest, shoulders, triceps, via push-ups or an overhead/bench press.
4. **Pull (row)** — back and biceps, the balance to all that pushing.
5. **Carry** — pick up something heavy and walk. Underrated, brutally effective for whole-body strength.

Together these five hit every major muscle group. You do not need machines for each body part; compound movements do the work of many.

**Sets, reps, and how often**

Two full-body sessions a week is plenty to start. Three sets of five to eight reps per movement, with a weight that feels hard but doable on the last rep. Add a little weight when it gets easy. That progression — slightly more over time — is the entire secret.

**Form first, weight later**

Ego lifting is how beginners get hurt. Learn the movement light, film yourself, fix it, then load it. A private, unhurried setting helps enormously here — no queue for equipment, nobody watching while you practise. Self-service gyms like [GymHome](https://gymhome.cz) in Frýdek-Místek and Ostrava are ideal for this: book a slot, have the whole place to yourself, and drill your form without an audience.

**A note for fitness creators**

Filming form tutorials is far easier in an empty gym. [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) then dubs them into 50+ languages so your coaching reaches beginners everywhere.

Strength is not built by complexity. It is built by five simple movements, a little more weight over time, and showing up twice a week. Start there.
